answer: The defence rests on skeleton racing licence with track run history: runs logged at one track across many seasons. Forging 141 of these means building 141 separate run histories from scratch, and years of history cannot be bought in bulk. Verification runs against the issuer's own registry every epoch, so a forged entry is caught on the next check. The ripple check runs in the open: 141 fakes pay the full price 141 times, one honest agent pays once, and the plume trail in the ledger makes the oasis cost visible to everyone.
